subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Which Telegram formatting modes should OpenClaw support, and should a per-account value override the channel default across rich sends, legacy fallback, captions, edits, and draft previews?
rationale: The requested setting creates a persistent public configuration contract and determines escaping, rendering, and trust semantics; source evidence does not establish that one mode set or precedence rule is already approved.

options.title: HTML plus explicit plain-text mode
options.body: Keep current formatted behavior as the default and add a safe opt-in plain-text mode with one shared resolver across all outbound paths.

options.title: Add MarkdownV2 too
options.body: Support HTML, plain text, and MarkdownV2 only after defining escaping, chunking, entity, and preview behavior for every Telegram delivery path.

options.title: Keep delivery choice only
options.body: Retain the current rich-message versus legacy delivery configuration and decline a general formatting-mode API for now.

recommendation.title: HTML plus explicit plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Keep current formatted behavior as the default and add a safe opt-in plain-text mode with one shared resolver across all outbound paths.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties steipete directly to the formatter transition and Telegram/config surfaces where the public contract would be defined.
